He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball|Illinois State Redbirds]] and the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]], and was drafted 47th overall by the [[Orlando Magic]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== After a prep career at [[Shadow Mountain High School]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix]] and [[Simeon Career Academy]] in his hometown [[Chicago]], Reeves committed to [[Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball|Illinois State]] over offers from several other [[mid-major]] programs. ==College career== ===Illinois State=== Reeves was a key contributor for his first two seasons, earning a spot on the [[Missouri Valley Conference]] (MVC) all-bench team as a sophomore. He declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] but ultimately chose to return to the Redbirds for his junior season. In the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]], Reeves averaged a career-high 20.1 points per game And was named second-team All-MVC, however, the team was not successful and coach [[Dan Muller (basketball)|Dan Muller]] was fired. With the coaching change, Reeves decided to transfer to a winning program.{{cite web|first=Isaac|last=Bourne|title=Antonio Reeves: From mid-major star to Kentucky Wildcat standout|url=https://www.midmajormadness.com/2023/12/22/24008018/antonio-reeves-from-mid-major-star-to-kentucky-standout|website=MidMajorMadness.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=December 22, 2023|access-date=January 18, 2024}} ===Kentucky=== Reeves ultimately chose Kentucky and coach [[John Calipari]].{{cite web|first1=Jeff|last1=Borzello|first2=Paul|last2=Biancardi|title=Antonio Reeves transfers from Illinois State to play basketball for Kentucky Wildcats|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33815244/antonio-reeves-transfers-illinois-state-play-basketball-kentucky-wildcats |publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=April 27, 2022|access-date=January 18, 2024}}{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Hale|title=What to know about Kentucky basketball's newest incoming transfer Antonio Reeves|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2022/04/27/antonio-reeves-kentucky-basketball-transfer-brings-scoring-ability/7354419001/|website=[[Courier Journal]]|date=April 27, 2022|access-date=January 18, 2024}} As a senior, he mostly came off the bench for the Wildcats and ranked second on the team in scoring behind [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] [[Oscar Tshiebwe]] at 14.4 points per game. At the close of the season, Reeves was named the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) co-Sixth Man of the Year.{{cite web|title=Antonio Reeves Named Co-Sixth Man of the Year to Lead Wildcat League Honorees|url=https://ukathletics.com/news/2023/03/06/antonio-reeves-named-co-sixth-man-of-the-year-to-lead-wildcat-league-honorees/ |publisher=[[Kentucky Wildcats]]|date=March 6, 2023|access-date=January 18, 2024}} He again tested the NBA draft waters and considered another transfer, but ultimately chose to return to Kentucky for a fifth year granted to players whose eligibility was affected by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web|first=Cameron|last=Salerno|title=Kentucky: Senior guard expected to rejoin team after rollercoaster offseason|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/antonio-reeves-returns-to-kentucky-senior-guard-expected-to-rejoin-team-after-rollercoaster-offseason/ |publisher=[[CBS Sports]]|date=June 21, 2023|access-date=January 18, 2024}} Entering his fifth year, Reeves was named preseason second-team All-SEC.{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Fisher|title=Pair of Wildcats named Coaches Preseason All-SEC|url=https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/Article/antonio-reeves-justin-edwards-kentucky-basketball-coaches-preseason-all-sec-219381691/ |publisher=[[247Sports]]|date=November 2, 2023|access-date=January 18, 2024}} As the season wore in, Reeves emerged as a key player for the Wildcats and senior presence for their talented recruiting class. In January 2024, he was named to the 25-man [[John R. Wooden Award|Wooden Award]] midseason watch list in recognition of his performance, along with teammate [[Reed Sheppard]].{{cite web|first=Armando|last=Barry|title=Reeves & Sheppard listed on Midseason Wooden Award watch list|url=https://www.wymt.com/2024/01/12/reeves-sheppard-listed-midseason-wooden-award-watch-list/ |publisher=WYMT|date=January 11, 2024|access-date=January 18, 2024}} ==Professional career== On June 27, 2024, Reeves was selected with the 47th overall pick by the [[Orlando Magic]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]], however, immediately on draft night, he was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for two second-round pick swaps in 2030 and 2031.{{cite web|first=Terry|last=Kimble|title=Pelicans Jump Back Into Second-Round; Draft Kentucky Guard Antonio Reeves|url=https://www.si.com/nba/pelicans/pelicans-jump-back-into-second-round-draft-kentucky-guard-antonio-reeves-01j18gz0w88x|website=Sports Illustrated |date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 28, 2024}} On July 23, he signed with the Pelicans.{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans sign Antonio Reeves|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/antonio-reeves-guard-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-signed-072324|publisher=NBA |date=July 23, 2024|access-date=August 2, 2024}} Throughout his rookie season, he has been [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Birmingham Squadron]].{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Birmingham Squadron Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Birmingham-Squadron/59/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 12, 2025}} Reeves made his NBA debut on October 23, 2024, in a 123–111 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|title=Chicago Bulls at New Orleans Pelicans Box Score, October 23, 2024|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202410230NOP.html|website=BasketballRef|date=November 1, 2024|access-date=November 1, 2024}} On November 20, Reeves put up a career-high 34 points in a 128–100 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/pelicans-news-rookie-antonio-reeves-34-points-birthday-remember-cavaliers|title=Pelicans rookie has 34-point birthday to remember vs. Cavaliers|website=ClutchPoints|last=Dodson|first=Chris|date=November 20, 2024|access-date=November 20, 2024}} On July 3, 2025, Reeves was waived by the Pelicans.{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans waive Antonio Reeves|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/antonio-reeves-waived-guard-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-moves-july-3-2025|publisher=NBA |date=July 3, 2025|access-date=July 10, 2025}} Still, Reeves joined the Pelicans for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Pelicans announce NBA 2K26 2025 Summer League roster presented by Caesars Sportsbook|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/nba-2k26-2025-summer-league-roster-new-orleans-pelicans-draft-picks|publisher=NBA |date=July 6, 2025|access-date=July 10, 2025}} On July 26, 2025, Reeves signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Antonio Reeves To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-sign-antonio-reeves-to-two-way-contract|access-date=July 26, 2025|publisher=NBA |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
